title: Peace
tomorrow: at orientation a stranger says 'come with me sunday.' does Grace go?

cards: People who leave hand something on: the house keys, the shared playlist, a sweatshirt that still smells like them. What do you leave when you have nothing to leave?

At supper on his last night, as John tells it, Jesus leaves his friends one thing, and it's an odd choice: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.” Here's the puzzle. There is no peace that night.
Betrayal and arrest are close. Why give peace now?

teach.b: The next words solve it: “not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.”
The world's peace often means trouble is over: the bills paid, the fight done, the danger past. Jesus gives his on a night full of trouble. So this peace isn't the absence of storms.

teach.h: A GUARDED HEART IN A STORM.
teach.b: It's a guarded heart in the middle of one.

Paul writes about it from his bonds: “the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” Passeth all understanding: it won't always make sense to someone watching.
And keep means guard, like a sentry at a door. Then the second half of the puzzle.
After the resurrection, John says the disciples were together behind shut doors, afraid.
Jesus stands among them, and the first thing he says is: “Peace be unto you.” The gift from the supper, handed over again in person. Earlier on this path came making peace with others.
This peace is different: received, not made. My peace, he calls it. In some churches, people turn to one another during worship and pass it along: peace be with you.

how: In some churches the congregation shares 'the peace' during worship, greeting one another with 'peace be with you'; Christians pray for God's peace in hard times, some with John 14:27 or Philippians 4:7.

o: an agreement that ends a fight between two sides
a calm that guards the heart, even in trouble
the feeling you get once every problem is solved

behind shut doors, he says: “Peace be unto you.”

keep means guard: God's peace “shall keep your hearts and minds.”

games.q: a friend who's a nurse says the calmest people on a hard shift aren't the ones whose shifts are easy. which line fits what she's seen?
o: my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth.
peace comes once every problem is finally solved.
peace is a personality type; some just have it.
games.why: Jesus gives peace on his hardest night: a guarded heart in the storm, not a life with no storms.

practice: Close your eyes and let your shoulders drop. When a worry knocks, don't argue with it; let the words my peace I give unto you answer it, and come back to the breath. If you don't pray, simply rest in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Peace. A calm Jesus gives, not as the world gives, that guards the heart even in trouble.

carryVoice: Carry this: my peace, given on the hardest night, not after it. Day seventeen forty-five, done.
